_meta.note: Kill usage friction: every domain adapter ships its OWN skill (auto-triggers on that domain, runs the whole workflow: map -> deplint -> context). Today the code adapter has code-aware-planning (Seam-1-only) and the docs adapter has NO skill. This adds the docs skill, rounds out the code skill to cover Seam 2, and — the HeartBeat way — makes 'ship a skill' an ENFORCED convention via a skill-integrity gate: every plugin/adapters/<domain>/ must have a skill that references it AND names real, WIRED gate-examples proofs (so a skill can't rot or cite a vanished command). Then the convention is codified in the adapter recipe (build-a-domain-adapter.md) and adapters.md. Node-only tooling; not a parity surface. Spec-first (the integrity proof fails now because docs has no skill); adversarial review on both gates.

tasks.title: Author the skill-integrity proof (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/skill-integrity.sh (parameterizable like self-audit.sh: accept optional <adaptersDir> <skillsDir> <runTests> args, defaulting to the repo, so it can run against a fixture). For EACH domain dir under the adapters dir, it asserts PER ADAPTER: (a) at least one SKILL.md under the skills dir references that adapter (contains 'adapters/<domain>') — else the finding 'no skill for adapter <domain>'; (b) among the skills that reference it, they name at least one gate-examples/<name>.sh proof (a proofless adapter skill is a finding), and EVERY named proof both EXISTS and is WIRED (its basename appears in run-tests.sh) — else the finding 'proof not wired' / 'proof missing'. Proofs are counted PER ADAPTER (one adapter's proofs must not 'cover' another). Print SKILL-INTEGRITY-OK only when domains>=1 and findings==0 (no vacuous 0/0). Add a `--selftest` with REAL TEETH modelled on self-audit.sh --selftest: build a temp fixture tree and assert, by DISTINCT finding strings and rc!=0 PER CASE, that (i) an adapter with NO skill is caught (grep the 'no skill' message), and (ii) a skill that names an UNWIRED (or missing) proof is caught (grep the 'not wired' message); and that a good adapter+skill+wired-proof PASSES; only then print SKILL-INTEGRITY-SELFTEST-OK. set -euo pipefail + explicit exits. On the CURRENT repo the real run MUST fail (the docs adapter has no skill AND the code skill names no proof) — the spec-first reproduction.

tasks.title: Write the docs skill + round out the code skill
tasks.description: Create plugin/skills/docs-authoring/SKILL.md — YAML frontmatter (name: docs-authoring; a NARROW trigger description: use when planning a multi-section documentation/research WRITING project as a HeartBeat DAG and you want citation-aware task dependencies + cited-section context — NOT for general doc edits). Body: the zero-friction workflow — run plugin/adapters/docs/docs-map.js on the corpus to get the codemap, dep-lint the authoring DAG with the UNCHANGED plugin/adapters/code/deplint.js, wire plugin/adapters/docs/docs-context.js as the context_cmd; reference its proofs by name: docs/howto/gate-examples/docs-deplint.sh and docs/howto/gate-examples/docs-context.sh; note the boundary (node-only, advisory). Update plugin/skills/code-aware-planning/SKILL.md: (1) it must reference 'adapters/code'; (2) it MUST name its proofs by path — docs/howto/gate-examples/code-deplint.sh, code-map.sh, AND code-context.sh (required — else the skill-integrity gate keeps the code adapter red); (3) it must now TEACH Seam 2 (a real workflow paragraph: wire plugin/adapters/code/codegraph-context.js as the executor's context_cmd so the touched symbols' subgraph is fed to Stage B), not just mention the words — so both adapter skills are symmetric (plan + context). Do NOT touch deplint.js or the executors.

tasks.title: Wire the skill-integrity proof (T92)
tasks.description: Add node-suite group T92 to tests/run-tests.sh (after T91): check T92.1 runs docs/howto/gate-examples/skill-integrity.sh asserting SKILL-INTEGRITY-OK, and T92.2 runs its --selftest asserting SKILL-INTEGRITY-SELFTEST-OK. Guard appropriately (bash-only, no node needed if pure bash — but the check reads files, so it just needs a shell). Keep the whole node suite green.

GATE_SK.desc: Every domain adapter ships a skill that references it and names real, WIRED proofs (skill-integrity gate, with a teeth-bearing selftest); the docs skill exists and the code skill now covers Seam 2 as well. Enforced deterministically and wired into the suite.

review.prompt: Refute that SK is done. Does skill-integrity.sh genuinely check that EACH plugin/adapters/<domain>/ has a skill referencing it AND that the skill names proofs which both EXIST and are WIRED (grep run-tests.sh)? Could SKILL-INTEGRITY-OK print vacuously (0 domains, or a skill that cites no proof slipping through — is 'at least one wired proof per adapter' actually required)? Does the --selftest have real TEETH — does it catch (i) an adapter with no skill and (ii) a skill naming a missing/unwired proof, and would SKILL-INTEGRITY-SELFTEST-OK fail if the checker were hollow? Did the proof FAIL on the pre-work repo (docs adapter had no skill)? Is the docs skill's trigger description NARROW (won't fire on every doc edit)? Does the code skill now actually cover Seam 2 (context_cmd + codegraph-context), and does it name its proofs? Were deplint.js / the executors left untouched?

criteria.desc: skill-integrity passes: every adapter has a skill naming real, wired proofs (non-vacuous)

the integrity proof is wired into the node suite
the code skill now covers Seam 2 (the context hook / provider), not just plan authoring
the docs adapter now has a skill that references it
the integrity checker reports BOTH findings independently (missing-skill AND unwired-proof), not just an OK marker
the code skill names its real proofs (so the code adapter is enforced, and a red ska is disambiguated)

GATE_SD.desc: 'Ship a skill' is a documented step of the adapter recipe and adapters.md presents skills as the friction-killer; the docs stay prose-clean, the corpus sweep is unbroken, and referenced proofs are wired (self-audit).

review.prompt: Refute that SD is done. Does build-a-domain-adapter.md actually add a 'ship a skill' STEP (not a passing mention) that points at the skill-integrity enforcement, and does adapters.md present per-adapter skills as the last-mile friction-killer — without overclaiming? Do the docs pass prose-check (links resolve, no fake hb commands) and NOT break the count-pinned corpus sweep? Does self-audit still pass (referenced proofs exist+wired, parity ok)?
